title: 12-name watchlist · 4 November 2026, 16:00 SGT
summary: AWS announced a Malaysian AI-adoption program. Reuters updated its election-related market report with concerns about possible AI regulation; this is shared market context, not a new restriction or issuer earnings forecast. No new acceptance appeared in the twelve tracked SEC submission feeds during the review interval. All twelve saved regular closes and six-horizon return series are unchanged and are not live prices.
coverage_note: Review window: 4 November 2026, 12:00–16:00 SGT (04:00–08:00 UTC), with a 15-minute overlap from 11:45 SGT. Source checks were completed after the fixed 16:00 SGT cutoff. Prior editions, reports, source qualifications and calls remain unchanged in their archives. New company research is limited to the verified AWS release; the substantive Reuters update appears once as shared context. Coverage is partial, not a complete wire or issuer-news census.
price_basis: Main prices are USD completed regular-session observations for 3 November 2026 at 16:00 EST (4 November 05:00 SGT), with original vendor timestamps preserved. Daily change compares the 2 November ordinary close. These are saved prior closes, not live or exact 16:00 SGT prices. The unchanged separate after-hours observations in company notes are dated 3 November 19:59 EST (4 November 08:59 SGT), except Berkshire at 19:55 EST (08:55 SGT). Their changes compare the regular close and never replace adjusted-close return endpoints. No premarket observation is included. TSM is the US-listed USD ADR.
return_basis: Cumulative return = 100 × (3 November 2026 adjusted close ÷ baseline adjusted close − 1). The 1–6 calendar-month baselines are 2 October, 3 September, 3 August, 2 July, 3 June and 1 May 2026. October 3 and May 3 fall on weekends; July 3 is the observed US Independence Day market holiday, so preceding sessions are used. All 72 dated inputs were independently checked. Adjusted closes incorporate split and dividend/distribution adjustments; ordinary previous closes remain separate. These are cumulative returns before fees and taxes, not six individual monthly returns.
caveats: All 12 regular and previous closes and all 72 dated adjusted-close baselines were freshly reconfirmed. Every daily, cumulative and separate after-hours percentage was independently recomputed; numeric regular-price and return fields are unchanged.

Search-indexed historical observations can lag vendor changes. Direct Yahoo retrieval was rate-limited; accessible indexed histories and other public history sources were checked, with stale or differently adjusted alternatives rejected. Original source links and provider-adjusted inputs remain attached to every horizon.

Optional Yahoo Blue Ocean overnight observations displayed clock times but required calendar-date inference from page context. They are excluded rather than assigned unverified dates. The precisely dated regular-close and after-hours observations are separate from subsequent market news.

We could not independently verify a comprehensive issuer-news feed for every company. Apple, Alphabet, Meta and Micron list-rendering gaps and Broadcom/TSMC homepage limitations are stated in their company notes.

The AWS page displays 3 November, while its body dateline and structured publication timestamp identify 4 November at 07:00 UTC. The discrepancy is disclosed; program targets do not establish new paid revenue.

The Reuters story originated in the overlap at 03:50:39 UTC. Its visible update is 07:33 GMT with minute precision, while structured metadata repeats the original timestamp. The substantive updated text is retained with that qualification.

Earlier AMD, Tesla, Berkshire and Meta developments are not repeated as new. The unresolved AMD source-number discrepancy and other prior qualifications remain in the earlier reports; no correction or new settlement confirmation was verified.
All twelve SEC recent-submission feeds were checked after the cutoff. This is not a complete census of third-party ownership filings or company announcements.
Quiet names have no newly verified company-specific narrative in this edition; that does not establish that no news occurred.
Watch only: no user holding, executed trade, buy call or recommendation is implied. No private diary, brokerage record, personal account information or restricted screenshot is included.

rows.name: Amazon

research.headline: AWS launches Malaysian public-sector and SME AI program
facts: AWS announced Semarak AI Malaysia. It plans Amazon Quick access for up to 445,000 government officers; GovHub, powered by Kiro, starts with a 500-developer pilot in 2026 and targets 4,000 developers by 2028.
The SME program aims to onboard 10,000 businesses by 2028, with eligible participants offered six months of complimentary Quick and Kiro access.
Structured publication time: 4 November 07:00 UTC. The body says 4 November; the page label says 3 November.
research.analysis: This expands AWS distribution and AI adoption in Malaysia. The release does not quantify incremental revenue, contract value or near-term earnings impact.
research.risks: Targets and pilot sizes are not realized paid subscriptions. Do not describe the previously announced MYR29.2 billion country commitment as new spending.
research.next_watch: Pilot rollout, adoption and conversion to paid workloads through 2028.
